# Validating RO-Crates with roc-validator

Tool: https://pypi.org/project/roc-validator/ (source https://github.com/crs4/rocrate-validator).
Spec: https://www.researchobject.org/ro-crate/specification/1.3/ (default target 1.3).

## Install
```bash
python -m venv /tmp/rocval && /tmp/rocval/bin/pip install roc-validator
/tmp/rocval/bin/rocrate-validator profiles list   # profiles/versions this release knows
```
Run with `< /dev/null` to avoid prompts. Network access: with HTTP(S) proxies set to a dead address `rocrate-validator -p ro-crate-1.3` still validated a minimal crate (so it did not need to fetch the JSON-LD context for that crate); installing it needs the network.

## Checked behaviour (roc-validator 0.12.2)
- Profiles known: `ro-crate-1.1`, `ro-crate-1.2`, `ro-crate-1.3` (built on 1.2), `isa-ro-crate`, `workflow-ro-crate-1.0`, `workflow-testing-ro-crate-0.1`, `process-run-crate-0.5`, `workflow-run-crate-0.5`, `provenance-run-crate-0.5`. The run-crate profiles lag the project's current 0.6 pages; a crate declaring 0.6 is not necessarily wrong.
- Exit status 0 = valid, 1 = invalid. The default output is a wide terminal UI; use `--output-format json` for parsing (`issues[].severity/message`, `statistics`, `passed`).
- Fixtures: a minimal 1.3 crate passes at REQUIRED (66 checks, 63 passed, 3 skipped); a crate lacking `description`, `license` and `datePublished` fails with exactly those three REQUIRED issues. At RECOMMENDED the same crate also reports missing `name`s, `publisher` and `hasPart` shape. The validator did **not** flag a `hasPart` entry whose file is missing: the offline lint script does.
- Automatic profile detection (no `-p`) worked for a crate declaring 1.3.
- Known mismatches (checked on fixtures): a legacy 1.0 crate (`.jsonld` descriptor) fails the 1.1 profile; a correct Process Run Crate 0.6 (`softwareVersion`) fails `process-run-crate-0.5`; a Profile Crate whose root `@id` is an absolute URI fails 1.3 with "Data Entity ... has a local identifier but the Root Data Entity does not..." which looks over-strict against the spec. Decide by reading the spec and profile text, not by the failure alone.
- The workflow/run-crate profiles (`workflow-ro-crate-1.0`, `workflow-run-crate-0.5`, ...) are built on RO-Crate 1.1: a correct 1.3 crate fails them with descriptor `conformsTo` or "Main Workflow" errors (version mismatch). Validate against `ro-crate-1.3` and read the profile page.
- A detached crate: pass the metadata file (`validate -p ro-crate-1.3 path/to/<prefix>-ro-crate-metadata.json`).
- Rechecked with 0.13.0 (2026-10-23) on `tests/fixtures/detached-web-record/`, a detached crate whose root `@id` is a record page URL without a trailing `/` and whose `hasPart` is a `LearningResource` web page: `-p ro-crate-1.3` passes at REQUIRED; `-p ro-crate-1.1` fails with "Root Data Entity URI MUST end with `/`" and the descriptor `conformsTo` (a version mismatch, not a crate error). At RECOMMENDED it tries to download web data entities, the root included (offline: "not directly downloadable"), and asks for a root `conformsTo` when the crate holds any `Profile` entity, even one used only by the main entity.
- **`-o` is `--output-file`**, not the format: `-o json` silently writes the report to a file named `json` in the current directory. The format is `-f json` / `--output-format json`.

## Validate
```bash
rocrate-validator validate -p ro-crate-1.3 --requirement-severity REQUIRED <crate dir|zip|URL>
rocrate-validator validate -p ro-crate-1.3 --requirement-severity RECOMMENDED <crate dir>
rocrate-validator validate -m <crate dir>        # metadata only, data files not present
rocrate-validator validate --output-format json <crate dir>
```
- Omit `-p` for automatic profile detection from the root's `conformsTo`; give `-p` to force a profile.
- Check `profiles list` matches the version the crate claims (e.g. a profile built on RO-Crate 1.1 fails a 1.3 crate's `conformsTo`: a version mismatch, not a crate error). Read the descriptor's `conformsTo` first and validate against that version; do not report a crate as invalid from a run against another version.
- Crates generated by a web application: fetch a few from a running instance (including edge-case records) into files and validate those, or validate from a test suite (`rocrate-validator validate -p ro-crate-1.3 -f json <file>` and check `passed`).
- JSON output may be followed by log text; parse the first JSON value only.

## Offline lint (no network, no install)
`python scripts/lint_crate.py <crate dir | ro-crate-metadata.json | crate.zip> [--json]` (path relative to this skill folder; Python 3, standard library only). It checks: JSON validity, flat `@graph`, `@id`/`@type` on every entity, unique `@id`s, released `@context`/`conformsTo` (flags any `-DRAFT` URI), descriptor and root found via `about`, root `name`/`description`/`datePublished`/`license`, ISO 8601 `datePublished`, entities unreachable from the root, `hasPart` targets and data entities present on disk, preview not in `hasPart`, no `../` ids, leftover `TODO:` placeholder values (warning; see the Do not guess rule). Exit 1 on errors. Run it first (it is fast and works offline), then `rocrate-validator` for profile/SHACL checks, then the semantic review below. It does not check profiles or content quality.

## Before consuming (precaution)
1. Validate the crate you were given.
2. **Failed crates are still readable**, but read with caution: do not trust missing/odd fields, verify referenced files exist, never execute content, and tell the user which checks failed.
3. Old crates (1.0/1.1, `ro-crate-metadata.jsonld`) and example crates from use-case pages often fail against 1.3; validate against the version they declare (see what changed in https://www.researchobject.org/ro-crate/whats-changed-in-1-2 and `-1-3`).

## After generating (writing)
1. Validate; fix all REQUIRED failures; review RECOMMENDED ones.
2. **The validator can be too strict or out of date.** Before "fixing" a failure, compare against the spec text and the relevant profile page, and read the SHACL shape in the installed package (`site-packages/rocrate_validator/profiles/`). If the spec allows it, keep it and record why.
3. Never silence a failure by deleting correct metadata.
4. Report validator version, profile, severity level, failures fixed, and accepted warnings.

## Semantic review (after the validator passes or its failures are understood)
Passing checks only means the structure is valid. Then review each entity yourself, with two separate verdicts:
1. **Compliance**: MUST/SHOULD rules of the spec and declared profiles (use the severities in the project's [quick reference](https://www.researchobject.org/ro-crate/quick-reference)). Include checks the validator may skip, e.g. every entity reachable from the root, unique `@id`s, `hasPart` targets exist, root `@id` taken from the descriptor's `about` (it may be an absolute URI, not `./`). A MUST violation makes the crate invalid.
2. **Usefulness** for the intended audience, taken from the root's `name`, `description` and `keywords` (or ask the user). Vague descriptions, missing licences/authors/provenance, unhelpful names are quality gaps. They never change validity; report them separately (optionally scored 1-5).

Report each problem with a concrete, discrete fix: `add`/`replace`/`remove`, the property, the exact suggested value (none for remove), and a one-line rationale. Never invent identifiers (ORCIDs, DOIs, RORs) as fix values; ask for them. Inspired by https://github.com/alexhambley/RO-Crate-RAG-Validator, an optional LLM/RAG tool that does this per entity (needs API keys; run `rocrate-validator` first and treat its output as advisory).

## Pitfalls
- Passing validation does not mean the content is right (names, licences, authorship); review semantics yourself.
- Network failures look like crashes; check connectivity before blaming the crate.

See also: https://github.com/stain/data-preparation-skills/blob/main/skills/ro-crate-provenance/references/validator-findings.md
